136@dataclass 

137class KGRebuildReport: 

138 """Non-fatal data-quality gaps observed while rebuilding KG aggregates. 

139 

140 Missing or unusable extraction material degrades the semantic aggregate, 

141 but rollback can still restore the hard provenance invariant by rewriting 

142 graph/vector/tracking source IDs to the surviving chunks. Operational 

143 storage failures are not represented here; rollback policy propagates 

144 those failures so its journal remains retryable. 

145 

146 Known degradation semantics: a degraded relationship preserves its stored 

147 ``weight`` as-is — without per-chunk extraction cache the rolled-back 

148 chunk's weight contribution cannot be subtracted (precision is 

149 restored only by a full reprocess). The degradation is recorded in the 

150 persisted ``kg_recovery_warnings`` so operators can identify affected 

151 aggregates. 

152 """ 

153 

154 missing_cache_chunk_ids: set[str] = field(default_factory=set) 

155 unusable_cache_chunk_ids: set[str] = field(default_factory=set) 

156 referenced_chunk_ids: set[str] = field(default_factory=set) 

157 degraded_entities: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict) 

158 degraded_relationships: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = field( 

159 default_factory=dict 

160 ) 

161 

162 @property 

163 def has_warnings(self) -> bool: 

164 return bool( 

165 self.missing_cache_chunk_ids 

166 or self.unusable_cache_chunk_ids 

167 or self.degraded_entities 

168 or self.degraded_relationships 

169 ) 

170 

171 @property 

172 def surviving_chunk_ids(self) -> set[str]: 

173 """Chunk ids involved in a degraded rebuild (owner-lookup scope). 

174 

175 Every specific bucket (missing/unusable cache, degraded aggregates) 

176 is a subset of ``referenced_chunk_ids`` by construction — missing = 

177 referenced minus cached, unusable/degraded are recorded per rebuild 

178 target — so the union is simply the full referenced set whenever any 

179 degradation was recorded, and empty otherwise. 

180 """ 

181 return set(self.referenced_chunk_ids) if self.has_warnings else set()

184def _get_relationship_vdb_timeout_seconds(global_config: dict[str, Any]) -> float: 

185 """Derive a defensive timeout for relation VDB upserts. 

186 

187 Rationale: 

188 - `knowledge_graph_inst.upsert_edge()` for the default NetworkX storage is in-memory and fast. 

189 - `relationships_vdb.upsert()` performs embedding calls and remote I/O, which is the more likely 

190 point of silent stalls during relation merge. 

191 """ 

192 configured = global_config.get("default_embedding_timeout") 

193 try: 

194 base_timeout = float(configured) 

195 except (TypeError, ValueError): 

196 base_timeout = 30.0 

197 # Keep a fixed lower bound high enough to avoid false positives on slow providers. 

198 return max(base_timeout * 3, 120.0)

209def _truncate_entity_identifier( 

210 identifier: str, 

211 limit: int, 

212 chunk_key: str, 

213 identifier_role: str, 

214 byte_limit: int = DEFAULT_ENTITY_NAME_MAX_BYTES, 

215) -> str: 

216 """Truncate entity identifiers that exceed the configured length limit. 

217 

218 Enforces both a character limit (``limit``) and a UTF-8 byte limit 

219 (``byte_limit``). Milvus validates VARCHAR ``max_length`` in BYTES, not 

220 characters, so a CJK identifier within the character limit can still 

221 overflow the field (e.g. 256 Chinese chars ~= 694 bytes > 512). The byte 

222 truncation cuts on a character boundary so the result stays valid UTF-8. 

223 """ 

224 

225 char_len = len(identifier) 

226 byte_len = len(identifier.encode("utf-8")) 

227 if char_len <= limit and byte_len <= byte_limit: 227 ↛ 230line 227 didn't jump to line 230 because the condition on line 227 was always true

228 return identifier 

229 

230 display_value = identifier[:limit] 

231 encoded = display_value.encode("utf-8") 

232 if len(encoded) > byte_limit: 

233 # Drop the partial trailing multi-byte char left by the byte slice. 

234 display_value = encoded[:byte_limit].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore") 

235 preview = identifier[:50] # Show first 50 characters as preview 

236 logger.warning( 

237 "%s: %s len %d chars / %d bytes > %d chars / %d bytes (Name: '%s...')", 

238 chunk_key, 

239 identifier_role, 

240 char_len, 

241 byte_len, 

242 limit, 

243 byte_limit, 

244 preview, 

245 ) 

246 return display_value

249def _truncate_section_context( 

250 heading_path: str, 

251 tokenizer: "Tokenizer | None", 

252 max_tokens: int, 

253) -> str: 

254 """Token-budget the `---Section Context---` breadcrumb before injection. 

255 

256 The breadcrumb is metadata layered on top of the (already chunk-sized) 

257 input text, so an unbounded heading chain could push an otherwise-valid 

258 chunk past the provider context window. When the path exceeds ``max_tokens`` 

259 we first collapse it to the **first** level (top-level document location) 

260 and the **last/leaf** level (the chunk's own, most-specific section), 

261 eliding the middle with ``first → … → leaf``. A token-dense path (emoji / 

262 byte-level tokenizers) can still exceed the budget even with one or two 

263 levels, so a hard token cap is always applied as a backstop — the returned 

264 string is guaranteed to fit ``max_tokens``. ``max_tokens <= 0`` or a missing 

265 tokenizer disables the cap. 

266 """ 

267 if not heading_path or tokenizer is None or max_tokens <= 0: 

268 return heading_path 

269 if len(tokenizer.encode(heading_path)) <= max_tokens: 

270 return heading_path 

271 levels = heading_path.split(HEADING_BREADCRUMB_SEP) 

272 if len(levels) >= 3: 

273 heading_path = ( 

274 f"{levels[0]}{HEADING_BREADCRUMB_SEP}…{HEADING_BREADCRUMB_SEP}{levels[-1]}" 

275 ) 

276 # Backstop: enforce the cap for token-dense short paths (and any collapsed 

277 # form that is still over budget). Prefer a trailing ellipsis when it fits, 

278 # but re-encode each candidate because custom/BPE tokenizers may tokenize 

279 # the suffix differently when it is appended to decoded prefix text. 

280 tokens = tokenizer.encode(heading_path) 

281 if len(tokens) > max_tokens: 

282 ellipsis = "…" 

283 ellipsis_token_count = len(tokenizer.encode(ellipsis)) 

284 if ellipsis_token_count <= max_tokens: 284 ↛ 289line 284 didn't jump to line 289 because the condition on line 284 was always true

285 for keep in range(max_tokens - ellipsis_token_count, -1, -1): 285 ↛ 289line 285 didn't jump to line 289 because the loop on line 285 didn't complete

286 candidate = tokenizer.decode(tokens[:keep]).rstrip() + ellipsis 

287 if len(tokenizer.encode(candidate)) <= max_tokens: 287 ↛ 285line 287 didn't jump to line 285 because the condition on line 287 was always true

288 return candidate 

289 for keep in range(max_tokens, -1, -1): 

290 candidate = tokenizer.decode(tokens[:keep]).rstrip() 

291 if len(tokenizer.encode(candidate)) <= max_tokens: 

292 return candidate 

293 return "" 

294 return heading_path 

295

297def _truncate_vdb_content(content: str, global_config: dict, content_label: str) -> str: 

298 """Clamp vector-store payload size to stay under embedding limits. 

299 

300 Uses the safe ``Tokenizer.truncate_by_token_limit`` contract: the result is 

301 independently re-encoded and verified to actually fit ``threshold``, so 

302 this no longer needs (or applies) a fixed heuristic safety margin — the 

303 old ``decode(tokens[:k])`` here had no such verification and was not 

304 guaranteed to round-trip back to <= ``threshold`` tokens for every 

305 tokenizer/content combination. 

306 """ 

307 if not content: 

308 return content 

309 

310 embedding_token_limit = global_config.get("embedding_token_limit") 

311 tokenizer: Tokenizer | None = global_config.get("tokenizer") 

312 if embedding_token_limit is None or tokenizer is None: 

313 return content 

314 

315 threshold = int(embedding_token_limit) 

316 if threshold <= 0: 

317 return content 

318 

319 try: 

320 span = tokenizer.truncate_by_token_limit(content, threshold) 

321 except TokenBudgetError as e: 

322 # Only possible if even the first Unicode code point can't fit the 

323 # embedding model's own context limit — not a real-world budget. 

324 logger.error( 

325 "%s VDB content cannot fit embedding limit %d: %s", 

326 content_label, 

327 threshold, 

328 e, 

329 ) 

330 raise 

331 

332 if span.end == len(content): 

333 return content 

334 

335 truncated_content = content[span.start : span.end] 

336 logger.warning( 

337 "%s VDB content truncated to %d tokens (embedding limit: %d, " 

338 "original length %d chars)", 

339 content_label, 

340 span.token_count, 

341 threshold, 

342 len(content), 

343 ) 

344 return truncated_content 

345

348 r"^\[(?:Image|Table|Equation) Name\](.+)$", 

349 flags=re.MULTILINE, 

350)

353def _parse_mm_display_name(content: str, fallback: str) -> str: 

354 """Return the friendly name embedded in a multimodal chunk. 

355 

356 Matches the leading ``[Image Name]…`` / ``[Table Name]…`` / 

357 ``[Equation Name]…`` segment produced by 

358 ``LightRAG._build_mm_chunks_from_sidecars`` — the producer-side 

359 contract is documented in that function's ``_render`` helper. Falls 

360 back to the sidecar id when the segment is missing or empty so 

361 callers never end up with a blank label. 

362 """ 

363 if content: 

364 match = _MM_DISPLAY_NAME_PATTERN.search(content) 

365 if match: 

366 candidate = match.group(1).strip() 

367 if candidate: 

368 return candidate 

369 return fallback

372async def _handle_entity_relation_summary( 

373 description_type: str, 

374 entity_or_relation_name: str, 

375 description_list: list[str], 

376 separator: str, 

377 global_config: dict, 

378 llm_response_cache: BaseKVStorage | None = None, 

379 truncation_tally: TokenLimitTruncationTally | None = None, 

380 truncation_write_ahead: Callable[[TokenLimitTruncationTally], Awaitable[None]] 

381 | None = None, 

382) -> tuple[str, bool]: 

383 """Handle entity relation description summary using map-reduce approach. 

384 

385 This function summarizes a list of descriptions using a map-reduce strategy: 

386 1. If total tokens < summary_context_size and len(description_list) < force_llm_summary_on_merge, no need to summarize 

387 2. If total tokens < summary_max_tokens, summarize with LLM directly 

388 3. Otherwise, split descriptions into chunks that fit within token limits 

389 4. Summarize each chunk, then recursively process the summaries 

390 5. Continue until we get a final summary within token limits or num of descriptions is less than force_llm_summary_on_merge 

391 

392 Args: 

393 entity_or_relation_name: Name of the entity or relation being summarized 

394 description_list: List of description strings to summarize 

395 global_config: Global configuration containing tokenizer and limits 

396 llm_response_cache: Optional cache for LLM responses 

397 

398 Returns: 

399 Tuple of (final_summarized_description_string, llm_was_used_boolean) 

400 """ 

401 # Handle empty input 

402 if not description_list: 402 ↛ 403line 402 didn't jump to line 403 because the condition on line 402 was never true

403 return "", False 

404 

405 # If only one description, return it directly (no need for LLM call) 

406 # Still sanitize: descriptions read back from existing graph nodes (or 

407 # injected by non-extraction producers) may carry XML-illegal control 

408 # characters that would crash the GraphML flush downstream. 

409 if len(description_list) == 1: 

410 return sanitize_text_for_encoding(description_list[0]), False 

411 

412 # Get configuration 

413 tokenizer: Tokenizer = global_config["tokenizer"] 

414 summary_context_size = global_config["summary_context_size"] 

415 summary_max_tokens = global_config["summary_max_tokens"] 

416 force_llm_summary_on_merge = global_config["force_llm_summary_on_merge"] 

417 

418 current_list = description_list[:] # Copy the list to avoid modifying original 

419 llm_was_used = False # Track whether LLM was used during the entire process 

420 

421 # Iterative map-reduce process 

422 while True: 

423 # Calculate total tokens in current list while periodically yielding so 

424 # a large merge does not monopolize the event loop in single-worker mode. 

425 total_tokens = 0 

426 # Tokenize each description once; the chunk-building pass below 

427 # reuses these counts instead of re-encoding the same strings. 

428 desc_token_counts = [] 

429 for i, desc in enumerate(current_list, start=1): 

430 tokens = len(tokenizer.encode(desc)) 

431 desc_token_counts.append(tokens) 

432 total_tokens += tokens 

433 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=32) 

434 

435 # If total length is within limits, perform final summarization 

436 if total_tokens <= summary_context_size or len(current_list) <= 2: 

437 if ( 

438 len(current_list) < force_llm_summary_on_merge 

439 and total_tokens < summary_max_tokens 

440 ): 

441 # no LLM needed, just join the descriptions 

442 # Sanitize for the same reason as the single-description 

443 # early return above: inputs merged from pre-existing graph 

444 # data are not guaranteed XML-safe. 

445 final_description = sanitize_text_for_encoding( 

446 separator.join(current_list) 

447 ) 

448 return final_description if final_description else "", llm_was_used 

449 else: 

450 if total_tokens > summary_context_size and len(current_list) <= 2: 450 ↛ 451line 450 didn't jump to line 451 because the condition on line 450 was never true

451 logger.warning( 

452 f"Summarizing {entity_or_relation_name}: Oversize description found" 

453 ) 

454 # Final summarization of remaining descriptions - LLM will be used 

455 final_summary = await _summarize_descriptions( 

456 description_type, 

457 entity_or_relation_name, 

458 current_list, 

459 global_config, 

460 llm_response_cache, 

461 truncation_tally=truncation_tally, 

462 truncation_write_ahead=truncation_write_ahead, 

463 ) 

464 return final_summary, True # LLM was used for final summarization 

465 

466 # Need to split into chunks - Map phase 

467 # Ensure each chunk has minimum 2 descriptions to guarantee progress 

468 chunks = [] 

469 current_chunk = [] 

470 current_tokens = 0 

471 

472 # Currently least 3 descriptions in current_list. 

473 # Reuse the per-description token counts computed above instead of 

474 # re-encoding every description a second time. 

475 for i, (desc, desc_tokens) in enumerate( 

476 zip(current_list, desc_token_counts), start=1 

477 ): 

478 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=32) 

479 

480 # If adding current description would exceed limit, finalize current chunk 

481 if current_tokens + desc_tokens > summary_context_size and current_chunk: 

482 # Ensure we have at least 2 descriptions in the chunk (when possible) 

483 if len(current_chunk) == 1: 483 ↛ 485line 483 didn't jump to line 485 because the condition on line 483 was never true

484 # Force add one more description to ensure minimum 2 per chunk 

485 current_chunk.append(desc) 

486 chunks.append(current_chunk) 

487 logger.warning( 

488 f"Summarizing {entity_or_relation_name}: Oversize description found" 

489 ) 

490 current_chunk = [] # next group is empty 

491 current_tokens = 0 

492 else: # current_chunk is ready for summary in reduce phase 

493 chunks.append(current_chunk) 

494 current_chunk = [desc] # leave it for next group 

495 current_tokens = desc_tokens 

496 else: 

497 current_chunk.append(desc) 

498 current_tokens += desc_tokens 

499 

500 # Add the last chunk if it exists 

501 if current_chunk: 501 ↛ 504line 501 didn't jump to line 504 because the condition on line 501 was always true

502 chunks.append(current_chunk) 

503 

504 logger.info( 

505 f" Summarizing {entity_or_relation_name}: Map {len(current_list)} descriptions into {len(chunks)} groups" 

506 ) 

507 

508 # Reduce phase: summarize each group from chunks 

509 new_summaries = [] 

510 for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks, start=1): 

511 if len(chunk) == 1: 511 ↛ 513line 511 didn't jump to line 513 because the condition on line 511 was never true

512 # Optimization: single description chunks don't need LLM summarization 

513 new_summaries.append(chunk[0]) 

514 else: 

515 # Multiple descriptions need LLM summarization 

516 summary = await _summarize_descriptions( 

517 description_type, 

518 entity_or_relation_name, 

519 chunk, 

520 global_config, 

521 llm_response_cache, 

522 truncation_tally=truncation_tally, 

523 truncation_write_ahead=truncation_write_ahead, 

524 ) 

525 new_summaries.append(summary) 

526 llm_was_used = True # Mark that LLM was used in reduce phase 

527 

528 # Update current list with new summaries for next iteration 

529 current_list = new_summaries

532async def _summarize_descriptions( 

533 description_type: str, 

534 description_name: str, 

535 description_list: list[str], 

536 global_config: dict, 

537 llm_response_cache: BaseKVStorage | None = None, 

538 truncation_tally: TokenLimitTruncationTally | None = None, 

539 truncation_write_ahead: Callable[[TokenLimitTruncationTally], Awaitable[None]] 

540 | None = None, 

541) -> str: 

542 """Helper function to summarize a list of descriptions using LLM. 

543 

544 Args: 

545 description_type: Type of the descriptions being summarized (entity or relation) 

546 description_name: Name of the entity or relation being summarized 

547 description_list: List of description strings to summarize 

548 global_config: Global configuration containing LLM function and settings 

549 llm_response_cache: Optional cache for LLM responses 

550 truncation_tally: Optional accumulator for token-limit truncation. A 

551 cut-off summary silently becomes the entity's/relation's persisted 

552 description, so it belongs in the same operator-visible record as 

553 truncated extraction. 

554 truncation_write_ahead: Optional hook awaited right after a truncation 

555 is recorded, BEFORE the summary is returned to the caller that will 

556 write it into the graph. Lets an additive caller (the custom-chunk 

557 path, whose resume never purges a failed attempt's mutations) make 

558 the record durable ahead of the mutation it warns about, so even a 

559 hard crash cannot leave a truncated summary in the graph with no 

560 journaled evidence. A hook failure propagates and fails this 

561 entity/relation — fail-closed into the caller's normal failure 

562 path. 

563 

564 Returns: 

565 Summarized description string 

566 """ 

567 use_llm_func: callable = global_config["role_llm_funcs"]["extract"] 

568 # Apply higher priority (8) to entity/relation summary tasks 

569 use_llm_func = partial(use_llm_func, _priority=DEFAULT_SUMMARY_PRIORITY) 

570 

571 addon_params = global_config.get("addon_params") or {} 

572 language = global_config.get("_resolved_summary_language") 

573 if language is None: 573 ↛ 574line 573 didn't jump to line 574 because the condition on line 573 was never true

574 language = addon_params.get("language", DEFAULT_SUMMARY_LANGUAGE) 

575 

576 summary_length_recommended = global_config["summary_length_recommended"] 

577 

578 prompt_template = PROMPTS["summarize_entity_descriptions"] 

579 

580 # Convert descriptions to JSONL format and apply token-based truncation 

581 tokenizer = global_config["tokenizer"] 

582 summary_context_size = global_config["summary_context_size"] 

583 

584 # Create list of JSON objects with "Description" field 

585 json_descriptions = [{"Description": desc} for desc in description_list] 

586 

587 # Use truncate_list_by_token_size for length truncation 

588 truncated_json_descriptions = await atruncate_list_by_token_size( 

589 json_descriptions, 

590 key=lambda x: json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False), 

591 separator="\n", 

592 max_token_size=summary_context_size, 

593 tokenizer=tokenizer, 

594 ) 

595 

596 # Convert to JSONL format (one JSON object per line) 

597 joined_descriptions = "\n".join( 

598 json.dumps(desc, ensure_ascii=False) for desc in truncated_json_descriptions 

599 )

674

696 )

699 entity_type = entity_type.replace(" ", "").lower() 

700

702 logger.warning( 

703 f"Entity extraction error: reserved entity type '{entity_type}' rejected in {context}" 

704 ) 

705 return None 

706 

707 return entity_type

876def _truncation_cause_suffix(result: Any) -> str:

886 if not is_truncated_response(result): 

887 return "" 

888 return " (response was truncated by the model's output token limit)"

1182 f"Extraction cache missing for {len(missing_chunk_ids)} of " 

1183 f"{len(all_referenced_chunk_ids)} referenced chunk(s); " 

1184 "rebuild may use structural fallback" 

1185 ) 

1186 logger.warning(status_message) 

1187 if pipeline_status is not None and pipeline_status_lock is not None: 

1188 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

1189 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = status_message 

1190 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, status_message) 

1191 

1192 if not cached_results: 

1193 status_message = "No cached extraction results found" 

1194 logger.warning(status_message) 

1195 if pipeline_status is not None and pipeline_status_lock is not None: 

1196 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

1197 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = status_message 

1198 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, status_message) 

1199 if rebuild_policy == "best_effort": 

1200 return report 

1201 

1202 # Process cached results to get entities and relationships for each chunk 

1203 chunk_entities = {} # chunk_id -> {entity_name: [entity_data]} 

1204 chunk_relationships = {} # chunk_id -> {(src, tgt): [relationship_data]} 

1205 

1206 for chunk_id, results in cached_results.items(): 

1207 try: 

1208 # Handle multiple extraction results per chunk 

1209 chunk_entities[chunk_id] = defaultdict(list) 

1210 chunk_relationships[chunk_id] = defaultdict(list) 

1211 

1212 # process multiple LLM extraction results for a single chunk_id 

1213 for result in results: 

1214 entities, relationships = await _rebuild_from_extraction_result( 

1215 text_chunks_storage=text_chunks_storage, 

1216 chunk_id=chunk_id, 

1217 extraction_result=result[0], 

1218 timestamp=result[1], 

1219 chunk_data=chunk_data_by_id.get(chunk_id), 

1220 ) 

1221 

1222 # Merge entities and relationships from this extraction result 

1223 # Compare description lengths and keep the better version for the same chunk_id 

1224 for entity_name, entity_list in entities.items(): 

1225 if entity_name not in chunk_entities[chunk_id]: 1225 ↛ 1228line 1225 didn't jump to line 1228 because the condition on line 1225 was always true

1226 # New entity for this chunk_id 

1227 chunk_entities[chunk_id][entity_name].extend(entity_list) 

1228 elif len(chunk_entities[chunk_id][entity_name]) == 0: 

1229 # Empty list, add the new entities 

1230 chunk_entities[chunk_id][entity_name].extend(entity_list) 

1231 else: 

1232 # Compare description lengths and keep the better one 

1233 existing_desc_len = len( 

1234 chunk_entities[chunk_id][entity_name][0].get( 

1235 "description", "" 

1236 ) 

1237 or "" 

1238 ) 

1239 new_desc_len = len(entity_list[0].get("description", "") or "") 

1240 

1241 if new_desc_len > existing_desc_len: 

1242 # Replace with the new entity that has longer description 

1243 chunk_entities[chunk_id][entity_name] = list(entity_list) 

1244 # Otherwise keep existing version 

1245 

1246 # Compare description lengths and keep the better version for the same chunk_id 

1247 for rel_key, rel_list in relationships.items(): 

1248 if rel_key not in chunk_relationships[chunk_id]: 1248 ↛ 1251line 1248 didn't jump to line 1251 because the condition on line 1248 was always true

1249 # New relationship for this chunk_id 

1250 chunk_relationships[chunk_id][rel_key].extend(rel_list) 

1251 elif len(chunk_relationships[chunk_id][rel_key]) == 0: 

1252 # Empty list, add the new relationships 

1253 chunk_relationships[chunk_id][rel_key].extend(rel_list) 

1254 else: 

1255 # Compare description lengths and keep the better one 

1256 existing_desc_len = len( 

1257 chunk_relationships[chunk_id][rel_key][0].get( 

1258 "description", "" 

1259 ) 

1260 or "" 

1261 ) 

1262 new_desc_len = len(rel_list[0].get("description", "") or "") 

1263 

1264 if new_desc_len > existing_desc_len: 

1265 # Replace with the new relationship that has longer description 

1266 chunk_relationships[chunk_id][rel_key] = list(rel_list) 

1267 # Otherwise keep existing version 

1268 

1269 except Exception as e: 

1270 report.unusable_cache_chunk_ids.add(chunk_id) 

1271 status_message = ( 

1272 f"Failed to parse cached extraction result for chunk {chunk_id}: {e}" 

1273 ) 

1274 logger.warning(status_message) 

1275 status_logger.log(status_message) 

1276 continue 

1277 

1278 # Get max async tasks limit from global_config for semaphore control 

1279 graph_max_async = global_config.get("llm_model_max_async", 4) * 2 

1280 semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(graph_max_async)

1284 rebuilt_relationships_count = 0 

1285 failed_entities_count = 0 

1286 failed_relationships_count = 0 

1287 structural_fallback = rebuild_policy == "rollback"

1289 async def _locked_rebuild_entity(entity_name, chunk_ids): 

1290 nonlocal rebuilt_entities_count, failed_entities_count 

1291 async with semaphore: 

1292 workspace = global_config.get("workspace", "") 

1293 namespace = f"{workspace}:GraphDB" if workspace else "GraphDB" 

1294 async with get_storage_keyed_lock( 

1295 [entity_name], namespace=namespace, enable_logging=False 

1296 ): 

1297 try: 

1298 degraded = await _rebuild_single_entity( 

1299 knowledge_graph_inst=knowledge_graph_inst, 

1300 entities_vdb=entities_vdb, 

1301 entity_name=entity_name, 

1302 chunk_ids=chunk_ids, 

1303 chunk_entities=chunk_entities, 

1304 llm_response_cache=llm_response_cache, 

1305 global_config=global_config, 

1306 entity_chunks_storage=entity_chunks_storage, 

1307 chunk_data_by_id=chunk_data_by_id, 

1308 structural_fallback=structural_fallback, 

1309 ) 

1310 rebuilt_entities_count += 1 

1311 if degraded: 

1312 report.degraded_entities[entity_name] = list(chunk_ids) 

1313 except Exception as e: 

1314 failed_entities_count += 1 

1315 status_message = f"Failed to rebuild `{entity_name}`: {e}" 

1316 logger.info(status_message) 

1317 status_logger.log(status_message) 

1318 if rebuild_policy == "rollback": 

1319 # A real storage/rebuild failure is retryable and must 

1320 # retain the custom-chunk journal. 

1321 raise 

1322 

1323 async def _locked_rebuild_relationship(src, tgt, chunk_ids): 

1324 nonlocal rebuilt_relationships_count, failed_relationships_count 

1325 async with semaphore: 

1326 workspace = global_config.get("workspace", "") 

1327 namespace = f"{workspace}:GraphDB" if workspace else "GraphDB" 

1328 # Sort src and tgt to ensure order-independent lock key generation 

1329 sorted_key_parts = sorted([src, tgt]) 

1330 async with get_storage_keyed_lock( 

1331 sorted_key_parts, 

1332 namespace=namespace, 

1333 enable_logging=False, 

1334 ): 

1335 try: 

1336 degraded = await _rebuild_single_relationship( 

1337 knowledge_graph_inst=knowledge_graph_inst, 

1338 relationships_vdb=relationships_vdb, 

1339 entities_vdb=entities_vdb, 

1340 src=src, 

1341 tgt=tgt, 

1342 chunk_ids=chunk_ids, 

1343 chunk_relationships=chunk_relationships, 

1344 llm_response_cache=llm_response_cache, 

1345 global_config=global_config, 

1346 relation_chunks_storage=relation_chunks_storage, 

1347 entity_chunks_storage=entity_chunks_storage, 

1348 chunk_data_by_id=chunk_data_by_id, 

1349 structural_fallback=structural_fallback, 

1350 ) 

1351 rebuilt_relationships_count += 1 

1352 if degraded: 

1353 report.degraded_relationships[(src, tgt)] = list(chunk_ids) 

1354 except Exception as e: 

1355 failed_relationships_count += 1 

1356 status_message = f"Failed to rebuild `{src}`~`{tgt}`: {e}" 

1357 logger.info(status_message) 

1358 status_logger.log(status_message) 

1359 if rebuild_policy == "rollback": 

1360 # A real storage/rebuild failure is retryable and must 

1361 # retain the custom-chunk journal. 

1362 raise 

1363 

1364 # Create tasks for parallel processing 

1365 tasks = [] 

1366 

1367 # Add entity rebuilding tasks 

1368 for entity_name, chunk_ids in entities_to_rebuild.items(): 

1369 task = asyncio.create_task(_locked_rebuild_entity(entity_name, chunk_ids)) 

1370 tasks.append(task) 

1371 

1372 # Add relationship rebuilding tasks 

1373 for (src, tgt), chunk_ids in relationships_to_rebuild.items(): 

1374 task = asyncio.create_task(_locked_rebuild_relationship(src, tgt, chunk_ids)) 

1375 tasks.append(task) 

1376 

1377 # Log parallel processing start 

1378 status_message = f"Starting parallel rebuild of {len(entities_to_rebuild)} entities and {len(relationships_to_rebuild)} relationships (async: {graph_max_async})" 

1379 logger.info(status_message) 

1380 if pipeline_status is not None and pipeline_status_lock is not None: 

1381 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

1382 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = status_message 

1383 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, status_message) 

1384 

1385 # Execute all tasks in parallel with semaphore control; on any failure 

1386 # every sibling is cancelled and drained before the first exception 

1387 # propagates (no background rebuild writes survive failure handling). 

1388 await wait_tasks_with_drain(tasks, context="KG rebuild") 

1389 

1390 # Final status report 

1391 status_message = f"KG rebuild completed: {rebuilt_entities_count} entities and {rebuilt_relationships_count} relationships rebuilt successfully." 

1392 if failed_entities_count > 0 or failed_relationships_count > 0: 

1393 status_message += f" Failed: {failed_entities_count} entities, {failed_relationships_count} relationships." 

1394 

1395 logger.info(status_message) 

1396 if pipeline_status is not None and pipeline_status_lock is not None: 

1397 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

1398 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = status_message 

1399 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, status_message) 

1400 

1401 if report.has_warnings: 

1402 logger.warning( 

1403 "KG rebuild completed with degraded recovery: " 

1404 "missing_cache_chunks=%d unusable_cache_chunks=%d " 

1405 "entities=%d relationships=%d", 

1406 len(report.missing_cache_chunk_ids), 

1407 len(report.unusable_cache_chunk_ids), 

1408 len(report.degraded_entities), 

1409 len(report.degraded_relationships), 

1410 ) 

1411 

1412 return report

1415async def _get_cached_extraction_results( 

1416 llm_response_cache: BaseKVStorage, 

1417 chunk_ids: set[str], 

1418 text_chunks_storage: BaseKVStorage, 

1419) -> tuple[dict[str, list[tuple[str, int]]], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]: 

1420 """Get cached extraction results for specific chunk IDs 

1421 

1422 This function retrieves cached LLM extraction results for the given chunk IDs and returns 

1423 them sorted by creation time. The results are sorted at two levels: 

1424 1. Individual extraction results within each chunk are sorted by create_time (earliest first) 

1425 2. Chunks themselves are sorted by the create_time of their earliest extraction result 

1426 

1427 Args: 

1428 llm_response_cache: LLM response cache storage 

1429 chunk_ids: Set of chunk IDs to get cached results for 

1430 text_chunks_storage: Text chunks storage for retrieving chunk data and LLM cache references 

1431 

1432 Returns: 

1433 A tuple containing the cache results grouped by chunk ID and the 

1434 corresponding text-chunk rows used for provenance fallback. 

1435 """ 

1436 cached_results = {} 

1437 chunk_data_by_id: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {} 

1438 

1439 # Collect all LLM cache IDs from chunks 

1440 all_cache_ids = set() 

1441 

1442 # Read from storage 

1443 requested_chunk_ids = list(chunk_ids) 

1444 chunk_data_list = await text_chunks_storage.get_by_ids(requested_chunk_ids) 

1445 for chunk_id, chunk_data in zip(requested_chunk_ids, chunk_data_list): 

1446 if chunk_data and isinstance(chunk_data, dict): 

1447 chunk_data_by_id[chunk_id] = chunk_data 

1448 llm_cache_list = chunk_data.get("llm_cache_list", []) 

1449 if llm_cache_list: 

1450 all_cache_ids.update(llm_cache_list) 

1451 else: 

1452 logger.warning(f"Chunk data is invalid or None: {chunk_data}") 

1453 

1454 if not all_cache_ids: 

1455 logger.warning(f"No LLM cache IDs found for {len(chunk_ids)} chunk IDs") 

1456 return cached_results, chunk_data_by_id 

1457 

1458 # Batch get LLM cache entries 

1459 cache_data_list = await llm_response_cache.get_by_ids(list(all_cache_ids)) 

1460 

1461 # Process cache entries and group by chunk_id 

1462 valid_entries = 0 

1463 for cache_entry in cache_data_list: 

1464 if ( 

1465 cache_entry is not None 

1466 and isinstance(cache_entry, dict) 

1467 and cache_entry.get("cache_type") == "extract" 

1468 and cache_entry.get("chunk_id") in chunk_ids 

1469 ): 

1470 chunk_id = cache_entry["chunk_id"] 

1471 extraction_result = cache_entry["return"] 

1472 create_time = cache_entry.get( 

1473 "create_time", 0 

1474 ) # Get creation time, default to 0 

1475 valid_entries += 1 

1476 

1477 # Support multiple LLM caches per chunk 

1478 if chunk_id not in cached_results: 1478 ↛ 1481line 1478 didn't jump to line 1481 because the condition on line 1478 was always true

1479 cached_results[chunk_id] = [] 

1480 # Store tuple with extraction result and creation time for sorting 

1481 cached_results[chunk_id].append((extraction_result, create_time)) 

1482 

1483 # Sort extraction results by create_time for each chunk and collect earliest times 

1484 chunk_earliest_times = {} 

1485 for chunk_id in cached_results: 

1486 # Sort by create_time (x[1]), then extract only extraction_result (x[0]) 

1487 cached_results[chunk_id].sort(key=lambda x: x[1]) 

1488 # Store the earliest create_time for this chunk (first item after sorting) 

1489 chunk_earliest_times[chunk_id] = cached_results[chunk_id][0][1] 

1490 

1491 # Sort cached_results by the earliest create_time of each chunk 

1492 sorted_chunk_ids = sorted( 

1493 chunk_earliest_times.keys(), key=lambda chunk_id: chunk_earliest_times[chunk_id] 

1494 ) 

1495 

1496 # Rebuild cached_results in sorted order 

1497 sorted_cached_results = {} 

1498 for chunk_id in sorted_chunk_ids: 

1499 sorted_cached_results[chunk_id] = cached_results[chunk_id] 

1500 

1501 logger.info( 

1502 f"Found {valid_entries} valid cache entries, {len(sorted_cached_results)} chunks with results" 

1503 ) 

1504 # each cache item is (extraction_result, create_time) 

1505 return sorted_cached_results, chunk_data_by_id 

1506

1508async def _process_extraction_result( 

1509 result: str, 

1510 chunk_key: str, 

1511 timestamp: int, 

1512 file_path: str = "unknown_source", 

1513 tuple_delimiter: str = "<|#|>", 

1514 completion_delimiter: str = "<|COMPLETE|>", 

1515 warn_on_missing_completion_delimiter: bool = True, 

1516) -> tuple[dict, dict]: 

1517 """Process a single extraction result (either initial or gleaning) 

1518 Args: 

1519 result (str): The extraction result to process 

1520 chunk_key (str): The chunk key for source tracking 

1521 file_path (str): The file path for citation 

1522 tuple_delimiter (str): Delimiter for tuple fields 

1523 completion_delimiter (str): Delimiter for completion 

1524 warn_on_missing_completion_delimiter (bool): Whether a missing 

1525 completion delimiter is worth a WARNING. Callers that already 

1526 reported the failure they are recovering from pass False so the 

1527 same failure is not announced twice; the missing delimiter is 

1528 still logged at DEBUG level for diagnosis. 

1529 Returns: 

1530 tuple: (nodes_dict, edges_dict) containing the extracted entities and relationships 

1531 """ 

1532 maybe_nodes = defaultdict(list) 

1533 maybe_edges = defaultdict(list) 

1534 

1535 if completion_delimiter not in result: 

1536 message = ( 

1537 f"{chunk_key}: Complete delimiter can not be found in extraction result" 

1538 f"{_truncation_cause_suffix(result)}" 

1539 ) 

1540 if warn_on_missing_completion_delimiter: 

1541 logger.warning(message) 

1542 else: 

1543 logger.debug(message) 

1544 

1545 # Split LLL output result to records by "\n" 

1546 records = split_string_by_multi_markers( 

1547 result, 

1548 ["\n", completion_delimiter, completion_delimiter.lower()], 

1549 ) 

1550 

1551 # Fix LLM output format error which use tuple_delimiter to separate record instead of "\n" 

1552 fixed_records = [] 

1553 for i, record in enumerate(records, start=1): 

1554 record = record.strip() 

1555 if record is None: 1555 ↛ 1556line 1555 didn't jump to line 1556 because the condition on line 1555 was never true

1556 continue 

1557 entity_records = split_string_by_multi_markers( 

1558 record, [f"{tuple_delimiter}entity{tuple_delimiter}"] 

1559 ) 

1560 for entity_record in entity_records: 

1561 if not entity_record.startswith("entity") and not entity_record.startswith( 

1562 "relation" 

1563 ): 

1564 entity_record = f"entity<|{entity_record}" 

1565 entity_relation_records = split_string_by_multi_markers( 

1566 # treat "relationship" and "relation" interchangeable 

1567 entity_record, 

1568 [ 

1569 f"{tuple_delimiter}relationship{tuple_delimiter}", 

1570 f"{tuple_delimiter}relation{tuple_delimiter}", 

1571 ], 

1572 ) 

1573 for entity_relation_record in entity_relation_records: 

1574 if not entity_relation_record.startswith( 1574 ↛ 1577line 1574 didn't jump to line 1577 because the condition on line 1574 was never true

1575 "entity" 

1576 ) and not entity_relation_record.startswith("relation"): 

1577 entity_relation_record = ( 

1578 f"relation{tuple_delimiter}{entity_relation_record}" 

1579 ) 

1580 fixed_records.append(entity_relation_record) 

1581 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=8) 

1582 

1583 if len(fixed_records) != len(records): 1583 ↛ 1584line 1583 didn't jump to line 1584 because the condition on line 1583 was never true

1584 logger.warning( 

1585 f"{chunk_key}: LLM output format error; find LLM use {tuple_delimiter} as record separators instead new-line" 

1586 ) 

1587 

1588 delimiter_core = tuple_delimiter[2:-2] # Extract "#" from "<|#|>" 

1589 delimiter_core_lower = delimiter_core.lower() 

1590 for i, record in enumerate(fixed_records, start=1): 

1591 record = record.strip() 

1592 if record is None: 1592 ↛ 1593line 1592 didn't jump to line 1593 because the condition on line 1592 was never true

1593 continue 

1594 

1595 # Fix various forms of tuple_delimiter corruption from the LLM output using the dedicated function 

1596 record = fix_tuple_delimiter_corruption(record, delimiter_core, tuple_delimiter) 

1597 if delimiter_core != delimiter_core_lower: 1597 ↛ 1599line 1597 didn't jump to line 1599 because the condition on line 1597 was never true

1598 # change delimiter_core to lower case, and fix again 

1599 record = fix_tuple_delimiter_corruption( 

1600 record, delimiter_core_lower, tuple_delimiter 

1601 ) 

1602 

1603 record_attributes = split_string_by_multi_markers(record, [tuple_delimiter]) 

1604 record_attributes = _normalize_text_extraction_record_attributes( 

1605 record_attributes, chunk_key 

1606 ) 

1607 

1608 # Try to parse as entity 

1609 entity_data = _handle_single_entity_extraction( 

1610 record_attributes, chunk_key, timestamp, file_path 

1611 ) 

1612 if entity_data is not None: 

1613 truncated_name = _truncate_entity_identifier( 

1614 entity_data["entity_name"], 

1615 DEFAULT_ENTITY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH, 

1616 chunk_key, 

1617 "Entity name", 

1618 ) 

1619 entity_data["entity_name"] = truncated_name 

1620 maybe_nodes[truncated_name].append(entity_data) 

1621 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=8) 

1622 continue 

1623 

1624 # Try to parse as relationship 

1625 relationship_data = _handle_single_relationship_extraction( 

1626 record_attributes, chunk_key, timestamp, file_path 

1627 ) 

1628 if relationship_data is not None: 

1629 truncated_source = _truncate_entity_identifier( 

1630 relationship_data["src_id"], 

1631 DEFAULT_ENTITY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH, 

1632 chunk_key, 

1633 "Relation entity", 

1634 ) 

1635 truncated_target = _truncate_entity_identifier( 

1636 relationship_data["tgt_id"], 

1637 DEFAULT_ENTITY_NAME_MAX_LENGTH, 

1638 chunk_key, 

1639 "Relation entity", 

1640 ) 

1641 relationship_data["src_id"] = truncated_source 

1642 relationship_data["tgt_id"] = truncated_target 

1643 maybe_edges[(truncated_source, truncated_target)].append(relationship_data) 

1644 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=8) 

1645 

1646 return dict(maybe_nodes), dict(maybe_edges)

1649async def _rebuild_from_extraction_result( 

1650 text_chunks_storage: BaseKVStorage, 

1651 extraction_result: str, 

1652 chunk_id: str, 

1653 timestamp: int, 

1654 chunk_data: dict[str, Any] | None = None, 

1655) -> tuple[dict, dict]: 

1656 """Parse cached extraction result using the same logic as extract_entities. 

1657 

1658 Supports both JSON and delimiter-based formats for backward compatibility. 

1659 Attempts JSON parsing first; if the cached result looks like JSON (starts with '{'), 

1660 uses the JSON parser. Otherwise, falls back to the traditional delimiter-based parser. 

1661 

1662 Args: 

1663 text_chunks_storage: Text chunks storage to get chunk data 

1664 extraction_result: The cached LLM extraction result 

1665 chunk_id: The chunk ID for source tracking 

1666 

1667 Returns: 

1668 Tuple of (entities_dict, relationships_dict) 

1669 """ 

1670 

1671 # Get chunk data for file_path from storage 

1672 if chunk_data is None: 

1673 chunk_data = await text_chunks_storage.get_by_id(chunk_id) 

1674 file_path = ( 

1675 chunk_data.get("file_path", "unknown_source") 

1676 if chunk_data 

1677 else "unknown_source" 

1678 ) 

1679 

1680 # Auto-detect format: try JSON first if the result looks like JSON 

1681 json_parse_reported_failure = False 

1682 if _looks_like_json_extraction_result(extraction_result): 

1683 # Parse once here and hand the payload down. The parse outcome, not the 

1684 # emptiness of what was extracted from it, is what decides below whether 

1685 # the failure being recovered from was already reported -- the two are 

1686 # different things, and a payload carrying the wrong schema 

1687 # ({"answer": "none found"}) extracts nothing while parsing perfectly. 

1688 parsed = tolerant_load_json_dict(extraction_result) 

1689 # Likely JSON format (from entity_extraction_use_json mode) 

1690 nodes, edges = await _process_json_extraction_result( 

1691 extraction_result, 

1692 chunk_id, 

1693 timestamp, 

1694 file_path, 

1695 parsed=parsed, 

1696 ) 

1697 # A successful parse (tolerant_load_json_dict's own non-empty-dict 

1698 # signal) is accepted even when it legitimately yields no nodes/edges. 

1699 if nodes or edges or parsed: 

1700 return nodes, edges 

1701 # Only an unrecoverable payload can reach here, and 

1702 # _process_json_extraction_result has already logged that failure. The 

1703 # delimiter parser below is a speculative rescue for a payload that 

1704 # merely looked like JSON, so its own "no completion delimiter" 

1705 # complaint would report that same single failure a second time; it is 

1706 # demoted to DEBUG for this call. 

1707 json_parse_reported_failure = True 

1708 

1709 # Fall back to traditional delimiter-based parsing 

1710 return await _process_extraction_result( 

1711 extraction_result, 

1712 chunk_id, 

1713 timestamp, 

1714 file_path, 

1715 tuple_delimiter=PROMPTS["DEFAULT_TUPLE_DELIMITER"], 

1716 completion_delimiter=PROMPTS["DEFAULT_COMPLETION_DELIMITER"], 

1717 warn_on_missing_completion_delimiter=not json_parse_reported_failure, 

1718 ) 

1719 

1720 

1721def _surviving_chunk_file_paths( 

1722 chunk_ids: list[str], 

1723 chunk_data_by_id: dict[str, dict[str, Any]], 

1724 global_config: dict[str, Any],

2384def _combine_descriptions_dedup( 

2385 already_description: list[str], new_descriptions: list[str] 

2386) -> tuple[list[str], int]: 

2387 """Merge stored and newly-extracted descriptions, dropping exact duplicates. 

2388 

2389 Stored fragments come first (preserving prior order), then new fragments not 

2390 already present. Deduplicating across stored *and* new (not only within the 

2391 new batch) prevents a re-extracted description from appending a duplicate 

2392 fragment on every reprocess or resume; it also collapses any 

2393 legacy duplicate fragments already stored. Returns the combined list and the 

2394 count of surviving stored fragments, used for accurate merge accounting. 

2395 

2396 Fragments are compared and stored *after* ``sanitize_text_for_encoding``: 

2397 stored descriptions were already sanitized before being persisted (the 

2398 single-description return and the join in ``_handle_entity_relation_summary`` 

2399 both sanitize), while a freshly re-extracted description is still raw. 

2400 Comparing raw-vs-sanitized would miss the duplicate whenever sanitization 

2401 changed the string (e.g. an XML-illegal control char was stripped), so 

2402 "dirty" descriptions would keep accumulating across reprocess. Sanitizing 

2403 here is idempotent, so the later sanitize calls are unaffected. Fragments 

2404 that sanitize to empty are dropped (they carry no information and would only 

2405 inflate the fragment count / emit ``<sep><sep>`` artifacts on join). 

2406 

2407 The two-phase walk is deliberate: ``already_fragment`` is captured after the 

2408 stored pass so it stays an accurate count of surviving stored fragments. Do 

2409 NOT collapse both phases into a single ``dict.fromkeys`` over the 

2410 concatenation — that loses the stored/new boundary the merge accounting log 

2411 depends on. 

2412 """ 

2413 combined: list[str] = [] 

2414 seen: set[str] = set() 

2415 

2416 def _add_sanitized(descriptions: list[str]) -> None: 

2417 for desc in descriptions: 

2418 sanitized = sanitize_text_for_encoding(desc) 

2419 if sanitized and sanitized not in seen: 

2420 seen.add(sanitized) 

2421 combined.append(sanitized) 

2422 

2423 _add_sanitized(already_description) 

2424 already_fragment = len(combined) 

2425 _add_sanitized(new_descriptions) 

2426 return combined, already_fragment 

2427

3477def collect_kg_merge_candidates( 

3478 chunk_results: list, 

3479) -> tuple[set[str], set[tuple[str, str]]]: 

3480 """Derive the full candidate entity/relation superset a merge may touch. 

3481 

3482 Write-ahead recovery anchor: before any graph/vector/tracking 

3483 mutation, the caller must be able to persist a durable candidate set in 

3484 ``full_entities`` / ``full_relations`` so a later purge/retry can discover 

3485 every object the merge might have written. The superset therefore 

3486 includes: 

3487 

3488 - every extracted entity name; 

3489 - every endpoint of every extracted relation (relation processing can 

3490 create missing endpoint entities, see ``_merge_edges_then_upsert``); 

3491 - every relation pair, normalized to sorted order (undirected graph). 

3492 

3493 The result is a candidate SUPERSET, not proof of existence: purge must 

3494 verify source ownership per candidate and treat absent objects as no-ops. 

3495 

3496 Args: 

3497 chunk_results: List of ``(maybe_nodes, maybe_edges)`` tuples as 

3498 produced by ``extract_entities``. 

3499 

3500 Returns: 

3501 ``(candidate_entity_names, candidate_relation_pairs)``. 

3502 """ 

3503 candidate_entities: set[str] = set() 

3504 candidate_relations: set[tuple[str, str]] = set() 

3505 for maybe_nodes, maybe_edges in chunk_results: 

3506 candidate_entities.update(maybe_nodes.keys()) 

3507 for edge_key in maybe_edges: 

3508 pair = tuple(sorted((edge_key[0], edge_key[1]))) 

3509 candidate_relations.add(pair) 

3510 candidate_entities.update(pair) 

3511 return candidate_entities, candidate_relations 

3512 

3513 

3514async def merge_nodes_and_edges( 

3515 chunk_results: list,

3517 entity_vdb: BaseVectorStorage,

3520 full_entities_storage: BaseKVStorage = None, 

3521 full_relations_storage: BaseKVStorage = None, 

3522 doc_id: str = None, 

3523 pipeline_status: dict = None, 

3524 pipeline_status_lock=None, 

3525 llm_response_cache: BaseKVStorage | None = None, 

3526 entity_chunks_storage: BaseKVStorage | None = None, 

3527 relation_chunks_storage: BaseKVStorage | None = None, 

3528 current_file_number: int = 0, 

3529 total_files: int = 0, 

3530 file_path: str = "unknown_source",

3534 | None = None, 

3535) -> None: 

3536 """Merge extracted entities/relations into the KG behind write-ahead anchors. 

3537 

3538 Phase order (discoverability before mutation): 

3539 0. Phase 0: Persist the full candidate superset to ``full_entities`` / 

3540 ``full_relations`` and flush both BEFORE any graph mutation, so a 

3541 crash mid-merge always leaves a durable recovery anchor that purge / 

3542 retry can discover the contributions from. Both rows are written even 

3543 when empty; a failure here aborts the merge before mutation. 

3544 1. Phase 1: Process all entities concurrently 

3545 2. Phase 2: Process all relationships concurrently (may add missing entities) 

3546 

3547 Args: 

3548 chunk_results: List of tuples (maybe_nodes, maybe_edges) containing extracted entities and relationships 

3549 knowledge_graph_inst: Knowledge graph storage 

3550 entity_vdb: Entity vector database 

3551 relationships_vdb: Relationship vector database 

3552 global_config: Global configuration 

3553 full_entities_storage: Storage for document entity lists 

3554 full_relations_storage: Storage for document relation lists 

3555 doc_id: Document ID for storage indexing 

3556 pipeline_status: Pipeline status dictionary 

3557 pipeline_status_lock: Lock for pipeline status 

3558 llm_response_cache: LLM response cache 

3559 entity_chunks_storage: Storage tracking full chunk lists per entity 

3560 relation_chunks_storage: Storage tracking full chunk lists per relation 

3561 current_file_number: Current file number for logging 

3562 total_files: Total files for logging 

3563 file_path: File path for logging 

3564 on_anchors_durable: Optional async hook awaited exactly once, after 

3565 both Phase 0 anchors are flushed and before the first graph 

3566 mutation. Lets the caller persist "this document may have touched 

3567 the graph from here on" (``doc_status.metadata.kg_write_state``) 

3568 in the one window where that statement flips, so a fail-closed 

3569 purge can distinguish a document that never reached the graph from 

3570 one whose anchors were lost. A raise propagates and aborts the 

3571 merge before any mutation. Not called when the anchor storages or 

3572 ``doc_id`` are absent (patch-mode merges, which carry their own 

3573 operation journal as the recovery proof). 

3574 truncation_tally: Optional document-scoped accumulator. Description 

3575 summaries are LLM calls too, so a too-small output budget truncates 

3576 them exactly like extraction; the merge folds its own count in so 

3577 the document's ``doc_status.metadata`` summary covers both stages. 

3578 truncation_write_ahead: Optional async hook awaited right after a 

3579 summary truncation is recorded, before the object carrying that 

3580 summary is upserted. For callers whose failure recovery is 

3581 ADDITIVE (the custom-chunk path: a resume keeps the failed 

3582 attempt's graph mutations), the record must be durable before the 

3583 mutation it warns about — a FAILED-transition stamp alone loses 

3584 the event on a hard crash. The pipeline's own merges do not need 

3585 it: a reprocess purges the previous attempt's contributions, so 

3586 nothing truncated survives to warn about. Receives the tally the 

3587 event was recorded into (the merge-local one, folded into 

3588 ``truncation_tally`` only when the merge publishes — after every 

3589 hook call has completed, because failing phases drain their 

3590 sibling tasks first).

3595 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

3596 if pipeline_status.get("cancellation_requested", False): 3596 ↛ 3597line 3596 didn't jump to line 3597 because the condition on line 3596 was never true

3895 edge_task_labels[task] = _format_relation_edge_label(edge_key) 

3896 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=32) 

3897 

3898 # Execute relationship tasks; failures cancel + drain every sibling 

3899 # before propagating (see wait_tasks_with_drain). 

3900 processed_edges = [] 

3901 all_added_entities = [] 

3902 

3903 if edge_tasks: 

3904 edge_results = await wait_tasks_with_drain( 

3905 edge_tasks, 

3906 context=f"relation merge {doc_id}", 

3907 task_labels=edge_task_labels, 

3908 ) 

3909 for edge_data, added_entities in edge_results: 

3910 if edge_data is not None: 3910 ↛ 3912line 3910 didn't jump to line 3912 because the condition on line 3910 was always true

3911 processed_edges.append(edge_data) 

3912 all_added_entities.extend(added_entities) 

3913 

3914 logger.info( 

3915 "Phase 2 relation processing completed for %s: edges=%d added_entities=%d", 

3916 doc_id, 

3917 len(processed_edges), 

3918 len(all_added_entities), 

3919 ) 

3920 await asyncio.sleep(0) 

3921 

3922 # NOTE: the recovery indexes are written (and flushed) in Phase 0, BEFORE 

3923 # graph mutation. The historical post-merge "Phase 3" write — which 

3924 # derived the rows from in-memory merge results and swallowed its own 

3925 # exceptions — is gone: a merge whose anchors cannot be persisted no 

3926 # longer mutates the graph at all. 

3927 

3928 finally: 

3929 # On EVERY exit — the inter-phase await points (sleep(0) yields, 

3930 # status-lock acquires) sit outside any narrower handler, and a 

3931 # cancellation landing there must still absorb the summary tally 

3932 # before the caller's failure bookkeeping recomputes from it. 

3933 _publish_summary_truncation() 

3934 

3935 log_message = f"Completed merging: {len(processed_entities)} entities, {len(all_added_entities)} extra entities, {len(processed_edges)} relations" 

3936 logger.info(log_message) 

3937 async with pipeline_status_lock: 

3938 pipeline_status["latest_message"] = log_message 

3939 append_pipeline_history(pipeline_status, log_message)

3942async def extract_entities(

3999 # Check if JSON structured output mode is enabled 

4000 use_json_extraction = global_config.get("entity_extraction_use_json", False)

4080 )

4094 async def _process_single_content(chunk_key_dp: tuple[str, TextChunkSchema]): 

4095 """Process a single chunk 

4096 Args: 

4097 chunk_key_dp (tuple[str, TextChunkSchema]): 

4098 ("chunk-xxxxxx", {"tokens": int, "content": str, "full_doc_id": str, "chunk_order_index": int}) 

4099 Returns: 

4100 tuple: (maybe_nodes, maybe_edges) containing extracted entities and relationships

4104 chunk_dp = chunk_key_dp[1] 

4105 # Strip parser-internal markup (<cite refid>, <drawing id/path/src>, 

4106 # <equation id>) before building the extraction prompt. The stored 

4107 # chunk content is left intact so query-time citations still resolve. 

4108 content = strip_internal_multimodal_markup_for_extraction(chunk_dp["content"])

4110 file_path = chunk_dp.get("file_path", "unknown_source")

4112 # Build the optional `---Section Context---` block from the chunk's 

4113 # heading breadcrumb. The marker/wrapping lives entirely in the prompt 

4114 # template; here we only produce the data and decide whether to inject 

4115 # it. Each level is char-capped inside format_heading_context, and the 

4116 # joined path is token-budgeted here so heading metadata can never push 

4117 # an otherwise-valid chunk past the provider context window. When the 

4118 # chunk carries no heading, the block is an empty string so the user 

4119 # prompt stays byte-identical to the no-context form. 

4120 heading_path = _truncate_section_context( 

4121 format_heading_context(chunk_dp), 

4122 extract_tokenizer, 

4123 DEFAULT_MAX_SECTION_CONTEXT_TOKENS, 

4124 ) 

4125 heading_context_block = ( 

4126 PROMPTS["entity_extraction_section_context"].format( 

4127 heading_path=heading_path 

4128 ) 

4129 if heading_path 

4130 else "" 

4131 )

4133 def _report_truncation(result: str, stage: str) -> None: 

4134 if not is_truncated_response(result): 

4135 return 

4136 location = f"chunk {chunk_key} in {file_path}" 

4137 # The server log keeps every occurrence with full identity; the 

4138 # bounded pipeline-status ring gets the first one plus the 

4139 # end-of-stage aggregate (see _publish_truncation_summary). 

4140 logger.warning( 

4141 f"Token-limit truncation during {stage} entity extraction " 

4142 f"for {location}" 

4143 ) 

4144 if stage_tally.record(stage, chunk_key): 

4145 status_logger.log( 

4146 f"Warning: token-limit truncation during {stage} entity " 

4147 f"extraction for {location}; further occurrences are " 

4148 f"reported as one summary at the end of extraction" 

4149 )

4151 def _report_cache_skip(cache_type: str) -> None: 

4152 """The extraction cache is off for this chunk; say so out loud. 

4153 

4154 ``use_llm_func_with_cache`` skips the cache write when the chunk 

4155 could not carry the reference to it. That is the safe direction, 

4156 but it means the extraction cache silently stopped working for this 

4157 document — the next run re-calls the LLM for these chunks. Reported on the 

4158 same discipline as truncation above: every occurrence to the server 

4159 log, the first one plus an end-of-stage aggregate to the bounded 

4160 pipeline-status ring. Synchronous and non-raising, per the 

4161 ``on_cache_skipped`` contract. 

4162 """ 

4163 location = f"chunk {chunk_key} in {file_path}" 

4164 logger.warning( 

4165 f"LLM {cache_type} cache write skipped for {location}: its cache " 

4166 f"reference could not be recorded on the chunk" 

4167 ) 

4168 first = not cache_skip_chunks 

4169 cache_skip_chunks.add(chunk_key) 

4170 if first: 

4171 status_logger.log( 

4172 f"Warning: LLM cache write skipped for {location} because its " 

4173 f"cache reference could not be recorded; further occurrences " 

4174 f"are reported as one summary at the end of extraction" 

4175 ) 

4176 

4177 if use_json_extraction: 

4178 # JSON mode: use JSON prompts and pass entity_extraction flag to LLM provider. 

4179 # The local must be bound explicitly: the text-mode branch below 

4180 # assigns this name, which makes it local to the whole closure 

4181 # (Python scoping is static), so the gleaning LLM call a few 

4182 # dozen lines down would otherwise read an unbound local here. 

4183 entity_continue_extraction_user_prompt = ( 

4184 json_continue_extraction_user_prompt 

4185 ) 

4186 entity_extraction_user_prompt = PROMPTS[ 

4187 "entity_extraction_json_user_prompt" 

4188 ].format( 

4189 **{ 

4190 **context_base, 

4191 "input_text": content, 

4192 "heading_context_block": heading_context_block, 

4193 } 

4194 ) 

4195 else: 

4196 # Text mode: use traditional delimiter-based prompts. The 

4197 # chunk-invariant system prompt is built once in the enclosing 

4198 # scope. The continue prompt stays per chunk because a custom 

4199 # prompt file may reference {input_text}; the default template's 

4200 # placeholders do not include it, but the call site keeps passing 

4201 # the kwarg for that override case. 

4202 entity_extraction_user_prompt = PROMPTS[ 

4203 "entity_extraction_user_prompt" 

4204 ].format( 

4205 **{ 

4206 **context_base, 

4207 "input_text": content, 

4208 "heading_context_block": heading_context_block, 

4209 } 

4210 ) 

4211 entity_continue_extraction_user_prompt = PROMPTS[ 

4212 "entity_continue_extraction_user_prompt" 

4213 ].format(**{**context_base, "input_text": content}) 

4214 

4215 final_result, timestamp = await use_llm_func_with_cache( 

4216 entity_extraction_user_prompt, 

4217 use_llm_func, 

4218 system_prompt=entity_extraction_system_prompt,

4220 cache_type="extract", 

4221 chunk_id=chunk_key, 

4222 text_chunks_storage=text_chunks_storage,

4224 response_format=({"type": "json_object"} if use_json_extraction else None), 

4225 llm_cache_identity=get_llm_cache_identity(global_config, "extract"), 

4226 ) 

4227 

4228 _report_truncation(final_result, "initial")

4230 history = pack_user_ass_to_openai_messages( 

4231 entity_extraction_user_prompt, final_result 

4232 ) 

4233 

4234 # Process initial extraction with appropriate parser 

4235 if use_json_extraction: 

4236 maybe_nodes, maybe_edges = await _process_json_extraction_result( 

4237 final_result, 

4238 chunk_key, 

4239 timestamp, 

4240 file_path, 

4241 ) 

4242 else: 

4243 maybe_nodes, maybe_edges = await _process_extraction_result( 

4244 final_result, 

4245 chunk_key, 

4246 timestamp, 

4247 file_path, 

4248 tuple_delimiter=context_base["tuple_delimiter"], 

4249 completion_delimiter=context_base["completion_delimiter"], 

4250 ) 

4251 

4252 # Process additional gleaning results only 1 time when entity_extract_max_gleaning is greater than zero. 

4253 run_gleaning = entity_extract_max_gleaning > 0 

4254 if ( 

4255 run_gleaning 

4256 and extract_tokenizer is not None 

4257 and max_extract_input_tokens > 0 

4258 ): 

4259 # Gleaning replays the initial extraction's user/assistant pair 

4260 # via ``history_messages`` and appends a "continue" instruction.

4267 gleaning_invariant_tokens 

4268 + sum( 

4269 len(extract_tokenizer.encode(msg.get("content", "") or "")) 

4270 for msg in history 

4271 ) 

4272 + ( 

4273 # Text mode only: the continue prompt embeds the chunk 

4274 # content, so its token count is chunk-specific. 

4275 len( 

4276 extract_tokenizer.encode(entity_continue_extraction_user_prompt) 

4277 ) 

4278 if not use_json_extraction 

4279 else 0 

4280 ) 

4281 )

4283 logger.warning( 

4284 f"Gleaning stopped for chunk {chunk_key}: " 

4285 f"Input tokens ({gleaning_token_count}) exceeded limit " 

4286 f"({max_extract_input_tokens})." 

4287 ) 

4288 run_gleaning = False 

4289 

4290 if run_gleaning: 

4291 glean_result, timestamp = await use_llm_func_with_cache( 

4292 entity_continue_extraction_user_prompt, 

4293 use_llm_func, 

4294 system_prompt=entity_extraction_system_prompt, 

4295 llm_response_cache=llm_response_cache, 

4296 history_messages=history, 

4297 cache_type="extract", 

4298 chunk_id=chunk_key, 

4299 text_chunks_storage=text_chunks_storage, 

4300 on_cache_skipped=_report_cache_skip, 

4301 response_format=( 

4302 {"type": "json_object"} if use_json_extraction else None 

4303 ), 

4304 llm_cache_identity=get_llm_cache_identity(global_config, "extract"), 

4305 ) 

4306 

4307 _report_truncation(glean_result, "gleaning")

4309 # Process gleaning result with appropriate parser 

4310 if use_json_extraction: 

4311 glean_nodes, glean_edges = await _process_json_extraction_result(

4313 chunk_key, 

4314 timestamp, 

4315 file_path, 

4316 ) 

4317 else:

4322 file_path, 

4323 tuple_delimiter=context_base["tuple_delimiter"], 

4324 completion_delimiter=context_base["completion_delimiter"],

4326 

4327 # Merge results - compare description lengths to choose better version

4329 glean_nodes.items(), start=1

4331 if entity_name in maybe_nodes: 

4332 # Compare description lengths and keep the better one 

4333 original_desc_len = len( 

4334 maybe_nodes[entity_name][0].get("description", "") or "" 

4335 ) 

4336 glean_desc_len = len(glean_entities[0].get("description", "") or "") 

4337 

4338 if glean_desc_len > original_desc_len: 4338 ↛ 4339line 4338 didn't jump to line 4339 because the condition on line 4338 was never true

4339 maybe_nodes[entity_name] = list(glean_entities) 

4340 # Otherwise keep original version 

4341 else: 

4342 # New entity from gleaning stage 

4343 maybe_nodes[entity_name] = list(glean_entities) 

4344 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=8) 

4345 

4346 for i, (edge_key, glean_edge_list) in enumerate( 

4347 glean_edges.items(), start=1 

4348 ): 

4349 if edge_key in maybe_edges: 

4350 # Compare description lengths and keep the better one 

4351 original_desc_len = len( 

4352 maybe_edges[edge_key][0].get("description", "") or "" 

4353 ) 

4354 glean_desc_len = len( 

4355 glean_edge_list[0].get("description", "") or "" 

4356 ) 

4357 

4358 if glean_desc_len > original_desc_len: 4358 ↛ 4359line 4358 didn't jump to line 4359 because the condition on line 4358 was never true

4359 maybe_edges[edge_key] = list(glean_edge_list) 

4360 # Otherwise keep original version 

4361 else: 

4362 # New edge from gleaning stage 

4363 maybe_edges[edge_key] = list(glean_edge_list) 

4364 await _cooperative_yield(i, every=8) 

4365 

4366 # No end-of-chunk cache-key attach here, by design. Each extract cache 

4367 # row is attached to this chunk BEFORE it is written, inside 

4368 # use_llm_func_with_cache; collecting the keys in memory and attaching 

4369 # them once at the end is precisely what orphaned them. See *LLM 

4370 # extraction cache reachability* in the contract doc, 

4371 # docs/design/PurgeRecoveryContract.md. Nothing here needs to re-attach: 

4372 # the extraction and gleaning calls above have each recorded their own 

4373 # key, and the multimodal injection below builds records from sidecar 

4374 # metadata without calling the LLM. 

4375 

4376 # Optional extraction-quality hook: the last word on what the LLM 

4377 # extracted from this chunk. Caller-facing contract, including why core 

4378 # never prunes on the hook's behalf, is documented under "Extraction 

4379 # Quality Hook" in docs/ProgramingWithCore.md. 

4380 # 

4381 # Deliberately placed BEFORE the multimodal injection below. That entity 

4382 # is core-generated, not LLM output, and it is linked to every surviving 

4383 # entity of the chunk: filtering afterwards would both expose it to 

4384 # rules written for LLM output (a "name must appear in chunk_text" 

4385 # grounding check deletes it) and leave the injected 

4386 # (multimodal_entity, rejected_entity) edges dangling, so the merge's 

4387 # endpoint upsert would re-create the very entities the hook rejected. 

4388 if kg_extraction_validator is not None: 

4389 validated = kg_extraction_validator( 

4390 chunk_key, 

4391 # The EXTRACTION-VISIBLE text: `content` already has the 

4392 # parser-internal markup stripped, and this reproduces the 

4393 # sanitize_text_for_encoding that use_llm_func_with_cache 

4394 # applies to the whole prompt. The invariant is that the hook 

4395 # sees byte-for-byte what sat between the ---Input Text--- 

4396 # fences of the prompt the provider received. strip=False 

4397 # follows from it: the chunk is a FRAGMENT sitting inside those 

4398 # fences, so its own boundary whitespace is interior to the 

4399 # prompt and stays model-visible, while the wrapper's strip only 

4400 # trims the template's ends. 

4401 sanitize_text_for_encoding(content, strip=False), 

4402 maybe_nodes, 

4403 maybe_edges, 

4404 ) 

4405 if inspect.isawaitable(validated): 

4406 validated = await validated 

4407 # Validate the shape before unpacking: a bare unpack accepts a 

4408 # two-key dict and silently binds its KEYS as maybe_nodes / 

4409 # maybe_edges, surfacing much later inside the merge as an 

4410 # unrelated-looking failure. 

4411 if ( 

4412 not isinstance(validated, (tuple, list)) 

4413 or len(validated) != 2 

4414 or not all(isinstance(part, dict) for part in validated) 

4415 ): 

4416 raise TypeError( 

4417 "kg_extraction_validator must return a (maybe_nodes, " 

4418 "maybe_edges) pair of dicts; got " 

4419 f"{type(validated).__name__} for chunk {chunk_key}" 

4420 ) 

4421 maybe_nodes, maybe_edges = validated 

4422 

4423 # Inject multimodal entity + associations for drawing/table/equation 

4424 # chunks. Placed inside the chunk's 

4425 # concurrency slot (rather than the centralized post-pass that used 

4426 # to live in utils_pipeline.augment_chunk_results_with_mm_entities) 

4427 # so each multimodal chunk benefits from the chunk-level concurrency 

4428 # already enforced by extract_entities. 

4429 sidecar_block = chunk_dp.get("sidecar")

4592 # only exposed on ties -- the persisted id/path fields are the unguarded

4651# Policy version of the query-answer cache (cache_type="query"). Bump it when the 

4652# meaning of an entry changes in a way the other key fields cannot express, so 

4653# entries written by older versions become unreachable instead of being served 

4654# under a key whose semantics have moved. v2 retires every entry written before 

4655# the _answer_cache_kv bypass below: such an entry may hold history-conditioned 

4656# text filed under a history-blind key, and entries record no history, so a 

4657# tainted entry cannot be told apart from a clean one. Only the answer cache is 

4658# versioned; keyword/extract/summary entries never see conversation_history. 

4659_ANSWER_CACHE_POLICY_VERSION = "query-answer-cache-v2"

4661 

4662def _answer_cache_kv( 

4663 query_param: QueryParam, hashing_kv: BaseKVStorage | None 

4664) -> BaseKVStorage | None: 

4665 """Return the storage backing the query-answer cache, or None to bypass it. 

4666 

4667 The answer cache key deliberately excludes ``conversation_history``: every 

4668 turn of a conversation carries a different history, so keying on it would 

4669 make each entry unique and turn a cache that is meant to be shared across 

4670 callers into a per-session one. But the history *is* handed to the model as 

4671 ``history_messages``, so an answer generated under it is not interchangeable 

4672 with the history-blind key it would be filed under. Requests carrying a 

4673 history therefore use neither side of the cache: 

4674 

4675 - they never write, so caller-supplied history cannot decide the answer that 

4676 other callers will be served for the same question; 

4677 - they never read, so a multi-turn caller is not served an answer that was 

4678 generated while ignoring its history. 

4679 

4680 Keyword extraction is unaffected and keeps using ``hashing_kv`` directly: it 

4681 derives keywords from the query text alone and never receives the history. 

4682 """ 

4683 if query_param.conversation_history: 

4684 logger.debug( 

4685 " == LLM cache == Query answer cache bypassed: conversation_history " 

4686 f"is set ({len(query_param.conversation_history)} message(s), " 

4687 f"mode:{query_param.mode})" 

4688 ) 

4689 return None 

4690 return hashing_kv

5223async def _get_vector_context( 

5224 query: str, 

5225 chunks_vdb: BaseVectorStorage, 

5226 query_param: QueryParam, 

5227 query_embedding: list[float] = None, 

5228) -> list[dict]: 

5229 """ 

5230 Retrieve text chunks from the vector database without reranking or truncation. 

5231 

5232 This function performs vector search to find relevant text chunks for a query. 

5233 Reranking and truncation will be handled later in the unified processing. 

5234

5236 query: The query string to search for 

5237 chunks_vdb: Vector database containing document chunks 

5238 query_param: Query parameters including chunk_top_k and ids

5241 Returns:

5244 # No broad try/except here -- mirrors _get_node_data/_get_edge_data, whose 

5245 # entities_vdb/relationships_vdb queries are also left to propagate. A 

5246 # backend query failure is not "zero relevant chunks": swallowing it here

5249 # dropped the vector-search branch while KG results kept flowing). 

5250 search_top_k = query_param.chunk_top_k or query_param.top_k 

5251 cosine_threshold = chunks_vdb.cosine_better_than_threshold 

5252 

5253 results = await chunks_vdb.query( 

5254 query, top_k=search_top_k, query_embedding=query_embedding 

5255 ) 

5256 if not results: 

5257 logger.info( 

5258 f"Naive query: 0 chunks (chunk_top_k:{search_top_k} cosine:{cosine_threshold})" 

5259 ) 

5260 return [] 

5261 

5262 valid_chunks = [] 

5263 for result in results: 

5264 if "content" in result: 5264 ↛ 5263line 5264 didn't jump to line 5263 because the condition on line 5264 was always true

5265 chunk_with_metadata = { 

5266 "content": result["content"], 

5267 "created_at": result.get("created_at", None), 

5268 "file_path": result.get("file_path", "unknown_source"), 

5269 "source_type": "vector", # Mark the source type 

5270 "chunk_id": result.get("id"), # Add chunk_id for deduplication 

5271 } 

5272 valid_chunks.append(chunk_with_metadata) 

5273 

5274 logger.info( 

5275 f"Naive query: {len(valid_chunks)} chunks (chunk_top_k:{search_top_k} cosine:{cosine_threshold})" 

5276 ) 

5277 return valid_chunks

5501async def _apply_token_truncation(

5506 """

5508

5510 the prompt) plus ``filtered_entities`` / ``filtered_relations`` (the matching 

5511 original records handed to chunk selection). 

5512 

5513 Ordering rule for any selector added here: the ``*_context`` lists are this 

5514 stage's output and the only importance ranking downstream sees. The 

5515 ``filtered_*`` lists MUST follow that same order -- stage 3 attributes a 

5516 shared chunk to the earlier-positioned record and allocates chunk quota by 

5517 list position -- so a selector that reorders must not leave the 

5518 ``filtered_*`` lists in stage-1 retrieval order. 

5519 

5520 A selector may reorder and drop, but must not invent: a ``*_context`` 

5521 record naming an entity or relation that was not in this stage's input 

5522 cannot be resolved back to an original, so it reaches the prompt but is 

5523 dropped from ``filtered_*`` with a warning.

5692 for relation_context in relations_context:

5694 if pair in filtered_relation_id_to_original: 

5695 continue

5697 if original is None: 5697 ↛ 5698line 5697 didn't jump to line 5698 because the condition on line 5697 was never true

5698 unresolved_relations.append(pair)

5700 filtered_relations.append(original)

5702 

5703 if unresolved_relations: 5703 ↛ 5704line 5703 didn't jump to line 5704 because the condition on line 5703 was never true

5704 logger.warning( 

5705 f"Dropping {len(unresolved_relations)} relation records absent from the " 

5706 f"pre-truncation map: {unresolved_relations[:5]}"

5711 "relations_context": relations_context,

5715 "relation_id_to_original": filtered_relation_id_to_original,

5719async def _attach_content_headings( 

5720 chunks: list[dict], text_chunks_db: BaseKVStorage | None 

5721) -> None: 

5722 """Backfill the ``content_headings`` field onto chunks in place. 

5723 

5724 Vector chunks never carry a ``heading`` field (chunks_vdb does not store it), 

5725 and the round-robin merge drops the entity/relation headings too. So we look 

5726 the chunks up by ``chunk_id`` in text_chunks storage and attach the parent 

5727 heading path. Only chunks that actually have parent headings get the field, 

5728 so empty paths are omitted from the JSON sent to the LLM. 

5729 

5730 Each level is char-capped inside ``format_parent_headings`` and the joined 

5731 path is token-budgeted against ``DEFAULT_MAX_SECTION_CONTEXT_TOKENS`` here — 

5732 mirroring the extraction breadcrumb (see ``_truncate_section_context``). The 

5733 query-context token truncation only keeps/drops whole chunks; it never trims 

5734 this metadata inside a retained chunk, so a deep heading chain (the per-level 

5735 cap bounds each level's length, not the number of levels) is bounded here. 

5736 """ 

5737 if not text_chunks_db or not chunks: 

5738 return 

5739 tokenizer = text_chunks_db.global_config.get("tokenizer") 

5740 chunk_ids = [c.get("chunk_id") for c in chunks] 

5741 chunk_data_list = await text_chunks_db.get_by_ids(chunk_ids) 

5742 

5743 def _backfill() -> None: 

5744 for chunk, data in zip(chunks, chunk_data_list): 

5745 if not isinstance(data, dict): 

5746 continue 

5747 headings = _truncate_section_context( 

5748 format_parent_headings(data), 

5749 tokenizer, 

5750 DEFAULT_MAX_SECTION_CONTEXT_TOKENS, 

5751 ) 

5752 if headings: 5752 ↛ 5744line 5752 didn't jump to line 5744 because the condition on line 5752 was always true

5753 chunk["content_headings"] = headings 

5754 

5755 # The whole loop is one submission, keeping submissions O(1) per request. 

5756 # It has to leave the event loop at all because this tokenizer is the 

5757 # long-lived one the storages captured at init, i.e. the SAME object every 

5758 # concurrent query uses — and two of its other consumers 

5759 # (_apply_token_truncation, process_chunks_unified) now run in the tokenizer 

5760 # executor. Left here, two concurrent queries would contend: one holding the 

5761 # tokenizer in a worker thread while the other waits for it on the loop. 

5762 await run_in_tokenizer_executor(_backfill) 

5763
